newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sun Life buys AXA Equity & Law.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sun Life buys AXA Equity & Law.

text.p: British insurance group Sun Life and Provincial Plc said on Wednesday it had bought AXA Equity & Law and AEL Investment Managers for 690 million pounds ($1.1 billion) from France's AXA-UAP.

Sun Life, majority owned by AXA-UAP, said in a statement that the enlarged group would be the third largest life insurance business in Britain and would have around 30 billion pounds of funds under management.

Sun Life said the package, which includes the 70 million pound acquisition of AXA Insurance Company Ltd, was expected to boost earnings in 1998 and generate annual cost savings of more than 37 million pounds.
Sun Life said it would issue 247.56 million new shares at 307 pence each to its parent to pay for the acquisitions, including 22.8 million shares for AXA Insurance.

The share issues will raise AXA-UAP's stake in Sun Life to 72.4 percent from 60.2 percent at present. Sun Life said it would have a market capitalisation of around 2.5 billion pounds based on a share price of 306p.

Sun Life said AXA-UAP planned to cut its shareholding to 65 percent of the enlarged issued share capital in two stages, selling an initial six million shares in the six months after completion of the deals. A further 53.6 million shares would be sold over another six-month period, the company said.
